categories.title: Getting started
categories.body: Create an agent and teach it your business.

categories.title: Channels
categories.body: Put your agent on your website, WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger.

categories.title: Integrations
categories.body: Connect your store, calendar, CRM and docs.

categories.title: Inbox, CRM and analytics
categories.body: Work with conversations, customers and reports.

articles.title: Create your first agent
articles.summary: Paste your website address and your agent reads your pages. No code is needed.
steps: Sign up and open Agents from the sidebar.
Create an agent and give it a name. Choose carefully: the agent name cannot be changed after it is created.
Paste your website address. Steps AI reads your pages, documents and FAQs.
Open the preview chat and ask the questions your customers ask most.
tips: The agent name is the one setting you cannot change later. Everything else can be edited.

articles.title: Add your business information
articles.summary: Websites, files and FAQs live in Resources and can be shared by every agent.
steps: Open Resources from the sidebar.
Add website pages, upload files or write FAQs.
Choose which agents use each resource.
Update a resource once and every agent that uses it answers with the new information.
tips: Keep prices, dates and policies current in your documents, so your agent answers with the latest information.

articles.title: Choose how your agent talks
articles.summary: Personas set your agent's role, tone and the things it must never do.
steps: Open your agent, then Intelligence, then Personas.
Pick a predefined persona or create your own.
Choose a tone: friendly, professional, direct or neutral.
Add guardrails, such as never quoting prices or never giving medical, legal or financial advice.
tips: You can generate a persona with AI from your homepage, the agent's role, your audience and your guardrails.

articles.title: Add the chat widget to your website
articles.summary: Copy one script, use a framework snippet, or install the WordPress plugin.
steps: Open your agent's channel settings and choose Website.
Copy the universal script, or the snippet for your framework.
Paste it into your site. Guides cover Wix, Webflow, Framer, Bubble and WordPress.
On WordPress, install the plugin instead. WordPress can remove script tags from pages, and the plugin avoids that.
Add allowed domains so the widget only runs on your own sites.
tips: If you leave allowed domains empty, the widget can be embedded on any website.

articles.title: Connect WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger
articles.summary: One Meta connection covers all three channels.
steps: Open Channels and choose WhatsApp, Instagram or Messenger.
Sign in with Meta and allow access to your business accounts.
Choose the agent that answers on each channel.
Send a test message from your own phone before customers do.
tips: You need admin access to the Facebook page to connect Messenger.
Messages that start a WhatsApp conversation use templates that Meta approves first.

articles.title: Customise the widget
articles.summary: Match your brand and keep the widget out of the way on mobile.
steps: Open your agent's Experience settings.
Set your logo, colours, light or dark theme and greeting.
Add up to five quick questions so visitors know what to ask.
Choose a floating widget or an inline search bar, separately for desktop and mobile.
Pick one of nine positions and when the widget appears: straight away, or after 5, 10 or 30 seconds, or one minute.
tips: Quick questions are the most useful field on this screen and the most often skipped.
On mobile, keep the bubble clear of your add-to-cart button.

articles.title: Publish a chat page
articles.summary: No website? Share a branded page with your agent on it.
steps: Open your agent's Site settings and create a page.
Add your logo, colours, welcome message and up to five suggested questions.
Add link cards for your catalogue, booking page or socials.
Preview on desktop and mobile, then publish and share the link.
tips: The page uses a public link on the Steps AI domain.

articles.title: Connect an app
articles.summary: Connecting is one step. Switching it on for an agent is the second.
steps: Open Resources, then Apps.
Choose the app and sign in, or enter your account details.
Switch the app on for each agent that should use it.
Ask a real question in the preview chat to check it works.
tips: An app that is connected but not switched on for an agent does nothing. This is the most common setup question.
Need an app that is not listed? Ask for a custom integration from the Channels area.

articles.title: Share order status with Shopify and your courier
articles.summary: Your agent reads the order from your store and the status from your delivery tool.
steps: Connect Shopify or WooCommerce from Resources, then Apps.
Connect your delivery tool: Shiprocket, Delhivery, DTDC, iThink Logistics or WareIQ.
Switch both on for your support agent.
Ask "Where is my order" with a real order number in the preview chat.
tips: The agent shares the status your store and courier report. It cannot change a delivery.

articles.title: Book appointments into your calendar
articles.summary: Use the booking skill with Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, Calendly, Cal.com or Square Appointments.
steps: Connect your calendar from Resources, then Apps.
Open your agent's skills and switch on Book appointment.
Choose the calendar this skill uses and the details to collect.
Write when the skill should be used, with examples.
tips: Each booking skill uses one calendar provider. You can connect several and choose per skill.

articles.title: Set up human handoff
articles.summary: Decide how long customers wait, what they see and who gets told.
steps: Open your agent's skills and switch on Hand over to a person.
Set the wait time: 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 1 minute or 2 minutes.
Write the fallback message customers see if nobody joins.
Add the people who get an email when a customer needs your team.
tips: If you add no email recipients, handoff emails are turned off.
On Instagram, replying from the Instagram app pauses the AI so it does not talk over you.

articles.title: Create tickets from conversations
articles.summary: Collect the details your team needs, then notify the right people.
steps: Switch on the Create ticket skill.
Choose the fields to collect, including custom fields such as order number or a photo.
Mark the fields that are required.
Add the email recipients who are told about new tickets.
tips: Tickets appear in the Tickets table of your CRM.

articles.title: Start with a workflow template
articles.summary: Cart recovery, order updates and team alerts, from menus, not code.
steps: Open Workflows and browse the templates.
Choose a template and rename it before you create it.
Review each step, such as waits, conditions and messages.
Switch it on. Workflows stay as drafts until you activate them.
tips: Most templates today are built for Shopify stores.
WhatsApp messages sent by a workflow use templates approved by Meta.

articles.title: Find the conversations that need you
articles.summary: Filter the inbox by channel, agent, tag, unread or starred.
steps: Open Inbox from the sidebar to see every agent and channel together.
Filter by channel or agent to focus.
Use tags to find conversations such as refund requests or new leads.
Star the conversations you want to come back to.
tips: Each agent also has its own conversation view.

articles.title: Use the built-in CRM
articles.summary: Customers, tickets and live requests, each in its own table.
steps: Open CRM from the sidebar.
Switch between Customers, Tickets and Live requests.
Choose the columns you want to see.
Add custom fields with a label, type and required setting.
tips: There is no limit on the number of contacts.
If your team already uses HubSpot, the agent can save leads there instead.

articles.title: Read your analytics
articles.summary: See volume, response time, channels and the hours customers message.
steps: Open Analytics and pick a date range.
Choose all agents or one agent.
Read the headline numbers: chats, messages, average AI response time.
Use the activity heat map to see which days and hours are busiest.
tips: Average response time measures the AI agent, not your team.
State-level location is available for website chats only.

articles.title: How credits work
articles.summary: A credit is not a reply. The model your agent uses sets the cost of each reply.
steps: Each plan includes a monthly number of credits.
Every reply uses credits. Faster, lighter models use fewer credits per reply than larger ones.
You choose the model for each agent.
Watch live usage on the Usage screen in your account settings.
tips: Extra credit packs expire at the end of your billing cycle.
See current plans and credits on the pricing page.

articles.title: What each plan includes
articles.summary: The Free plan is for trying the agent. Order tracking, handoff and channels start on Starter.
steps: Free: one agent and a small number of credits to try it out.
Starter adds order tracking, human handoff, channel integrations, ticketing, workflows and broadcasting.
Growth and Scale add more credits and deeper analytics.
Enterprise adds white-labelling, SSO and API access.
tips: Paid plans include unlimited agents.

articles.title: Cancel or change your plan
articles.summary: Cancel at any time. Your plan stays active until the end of the period.
steps: Open account settings, then Billing.
Choose Manage to change or cancel your plan.
Your plan stays active until the end of the billing period.
You can export your data for up to 30 days after your account ends.
tips: Payments are not refunded, and unused credits do not carry over.
